# **Scheduling Module** 

# Doctor’s Availability & Exceptions  Management  

# **Overview**

## **1\.  Document Information**

| Field | Placeholder |
| ----- | ----- |
| Module | Scheduling Module |
| Version | v1.0 |
| Date Created | 16th August 2025 |
| Last Updated | 15th October 2025 |
| Review | Product team in liaison with Engineering team |

## **2\. Purpose**

This workflow enables the facility Admin to add Location/Practioner/Healthcare Services’s roster to define their 

availability for patient appointments and set exceptions for unavailability. It ensures that only valid time slots are 

displayed to reception staff and patients for booking, improving scheduling efficiency and minimizing conflicts.

## **3\. Scope**

Covers creating weekly availability templates and configuring exceptions (unavailability).

## **4\. User Persona Context**

Facility Admins use this workflow to manage Locations/Practioners/Healthcare Services’ schedules in the CARE 

platform. They set up recurring availability and mark exceptions to avoid conflicts, ensuring patients and reception 

staff only book valid slots.

## **5\. Prerequisites**

### **5.1 System Requirement**

Facility Admin must be logged into the CARE platform with scheduling permissions.

### **5.2 Knowledge Requirement**

Familiarity with clinical working hours and personal availability.

## **6\. Expected Outcome**

* Availability slots created by the doctor will appear on the appointment calendar, in green colour  

                
              by template.

* Patients and reception staff will only be able to book appointments during the available slots.  
    
* Any configured exceptions will block bookings for specified times/dates.

## **8 Step-by-Step Instructions**

### **8.1 Creating Availability Slots**

#### 8.1.1 Login (Facility Admin) 

**Step 1**: Login to the CARE platform with your admin credentials.

![][image5]

**Step 2**: Select the associated facility from the **Facilities** list.

**![][image2]**

**Step 3**: List down various options including **Overview, Patient, Queues, Appointment, Services,**   
**Resources, Users, Billing, Settings.**

![][image6]

#### 8.1.2 Creating Availability Slots

**Step 4**: Click on **Services** option from the left hand menu and select the location which needs to be updated with the availability slots.Here in this case we are doing it for the OPD department for Outpatient consultations.   
![][image7]

**Step 5:** Select the schedule option from the menu options

![][image8]

**Step 6:** Click on **Create template** option   
![][image9]

![][image10]

**Step 7**: Enter a Template Name (*Example: Regular OP day*). Choose the Start and End Date for the 

schedule. 

**Step 8**: Define available Time Slots for each day of the selected week based on your working hours. A Schedule 

represents a block of time during which a doctor is available in an OPD  for patient appointments.

*Example: Morning OPD from 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM or Afternoon OPD from 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM.*

Each schedule can have multiple appointment slots depending on how you configure time and patient 

capacity.

Doctors can divide their working hours into multiple sessions to better organize patient flow.

*Example: Morning OPD → 09:00 AM – 01:00 PM, Afternoon OPD → 02:00 PM – 05:00 PM, Evening OPD* 

*→ 06:00 PM – 08:00 PM*

This way, patients can be booked only within the defined time windows, preventing overlaps and 

ensuring smooth management of appointments.

The **Auto-Fill Slot Duration button** automatically generates time slots within a time schedule based on 

the given slot duration and time range.

*Example: If session is for 09:00 AM – 01:00 PM, slot duration \= 3 minute → the system will* 

*auto-generate 80 slots (09:00, 09:03, 09:06, … up to 01:00 PM).*

**Slot Duration** defines how long each patient appointment lasts.

*Example: 3 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes or 30 minutes per patient.*

**Patient per Slot** specifies how many patients can be booked in the same slot. As in our case, as the patient footfall 

will be high, to save time a large number of patients can be booked for a particular slot. Say, if we know that for 

9am-11am slot, patient footfall will be 100, then we can book 100 patients per slot. *(useful for group consultations* 

*or quicker checkups) or even more number of Patients can be booked for a slot so that consultations can be quicker.* 

**Step 9**: Click **Save** to finalize and activate the schedule.        

### **8.2 How to Mark Exception (Unavailability)**

Exception allows users  to mark unavailable days to avoid the patient bookings.

**Step 1**: [Login and follow as per the instructions and do the below steps accordingly.](#7.-login-\(for-doctor’s-schedule-created-by-facility-admin\)) 

**Step 2**: Click **Exceptions** under **Availability**.         

![][image11]

**Step 3**: Click **Add Exception**.

![][image12]

**Step 4**: Enter **Unavailable Date(s)**, **Time Window**, and **Reason** ( Example: *“Conference”, “Surgery”* ).

**Step 5**: Click **Confirm Unavailability**.         

**Step 6**: Check the appointment calendar, those dates/times are now blocked from booking (Diagonal stripped lines).

### ![][image13]

### **8.2.1 Calendar quick action (mark a single-day exception):**

**Step 7**: In the right-side **Calendar**, click the **Date** you will be unavailable.

**Step 8:** Select **Add Exception**.  

![][image14]  
**Step 9:** Enter the **Time slot** and **Reason**.

**Step 10:** Click **Confirm Unavailability** and verify that bookings are blocked for that date/time.

Example: *Add an exception for **12-Aug, 10:00–13:00 (Department Meeting)**. No bookings will be allowed* 

*during that window.*

### *![][image15]*

### **8.3 How to Edit/Delete a Schedule**

**Step 1**: [Login and follow as per the instructions and do the below steps accordingly.](#7.-login-\(for-doctor’s-schedule-created-by-facility-admin\))   
       
**Step 2**: Locate the template you want to modify.               

**Step 3**: Click **Edit icon** to change **Template Name**, **Dates**, or **Time Slots**.![][image16]

**Step 4**: Click **Save** to apply changes.

**Step 5**: To remove a template entirely, click **Delete** and confirm there itself.          

**Step 6**: Verify the appointment calendar reflects your change (edited slots updated or template removed).

**Step 7:** To add another session with an existing Schedule Template,  click **Add another session**  in the **edit icon** and define the **Day** and **Time Slot.**

![][image17]  
**Step 8**: Confirm updates are visible on the calendar (only these windows will be bookable).

### **8.4 Manage Charges** 

As the OPD fee is constant for all patients, except a few exceptions like an MLC/Antenatal/New born/Relief camp, OPD fee can be added to the schedule of an OPD location. This will be automatically collected at the counter when a patient is registered, unless tagged as an exception like  MLC/Antenatal/New born/Relief camp.

**Step 1**:  [Login and follow as per the instructions and do the below steps accordingly.](#7.-login-\(for-doctor’s-schedule-created-by-facility-admin\))  

**Step 2**: Click **Manage Charges**.  
![][image18]

**Step 3**: Under Consultation Charge, click **Create**.

![][image19]

**Step 4**: Fill out required including **Title, Slug, Category, Pricing components** and then click **Create.**

![][image20]

**Step 5**: Fill out details like **Consultation Charge, Re-visit allowed days, Re-visit consultation charge** and then click **save**.

![][image21]

## **9\. Error Handling / Common Issues**

| Error Message / Issue | Possible Cause | Resolution |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Slots not visible on the calendar. | Template not saved or date range outside view | Reopen template, verify dates and Save; adjust calendar view range |
| There are bookings during this exception. | Trying to add the exception on the date of a scheduled appointment. | Add the Exception properly on another day or another time slot and then confirm unavailability. |
| Cannot create template. | Missing mandatory fields | Provide Template Name, Start/End Date, and at least one Time Slot. |
| Overlapping/duplicate slots | Multiple templates or sessions overlap. | Edit in Availability in My Schedules in Overview to remove overlaps, maintain one template/session per time slot. |
